chapter: Breakup, the 1940 band and the Navy
title: The Navy band never recorded; rehearsing at Treasure Island
summary: No recording was possible in the jungle clearings; the band was shaped up at Pier 92 in New York and Treasure Island.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did the Navy band record anywhere?
Never. We were never where we could record. We were playing in jungle clearings.
Even before you went away? Before you left . . .

Before we went away the band was nothing. We rehearsed it in Pearl Harbor. I mean, not in Pearl Harbor, but in Treasure Island. That’s where I really got it in shape. Or in Pier 92 in New York, which was a hellhole. By the time we were through with that, we were embarked on a train, and it took us two weeks to cross the country. We’d have to practice by ourselves in order to keep our chops up. Then we got to Treasure Island, and we could rehearse. I had to requisition a place to rehearse. Then you’d have sailors wandering in and out. It was a pain in the ass.
